title: Is this model worth $1 to you?
author: Rhaversen
selftext:
I made a pretty cool AI-assisted 3D model generator. The user is in control of what is created with natural language and can even edit it with 3D gizmos. This design cost $1 to create with the tool. For that price, could you see yourself using this tool to create 3D models?

For the record, I am not promoting my tool; I am only looking for feedback on its performance.

comments.author: 0DayMaker
comments.body: No. Meshy can make far better models for pennies. Also I get better results from opus 5 via the blender mcp sorry.

replies.author: Rhaversen
replies.body:
https://preview.redd.it/u6l2htbfe8nh1.png?width=1172&format=png&auto=webp&s=d9014e173ab26a4cfcb31baf2233f7c46a56ac8a

This was made with Gemini Pro and only cost 0.20$. The agent could keep iterating and adding detail, but it racks up the price. With better context handling, the price could come down too. The cool part is that you can iterate on the model continually, which is not possible with Meshy, and the agent adds parameters that you can edit manually to change the look of the model. Things like roof height, house width, and so on.

Currently, the price to performance is a little steep, that i agree with. But do you think it has potential if the tool became better?

comments.author: Neither_Berry_100
comments.body: That seems horribly expensive for an AI tool. There should be much better on the market.

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body: nah big bro a free ai pic and image to 3zjs (threesjs) can get u 10000% better

comments.author: EC36339
comments.body:
If you buy a $1 model from a "real" artist, you get the exact same $1 model that others have also paid $1 for.

No artist will make you a unique and exclusive model that you ask for and refine in several rounds for $1.
